rows.notes: The study is a Perspective/opinion piece (WIREs Water 'PERSPECTIVE'); the data availability statement says no new data were created or analyzed. It synthesises cited literature (Grafton et al. 2018, Perry & Steduto 2017, Pfeiffer & Lin 2014, Scott et al. 2014, World Bank Turpan reports) to argue that irrigation efficiency upgrades reduce return flows, reallocate water to 'high value' uses and complicate governance, and it proposes a water-justice governance framework. It reports no primary result of its own on drip irrigation, return flows, water availability for other users or governance; all examples (Kansas, Guadiana, Murray-Darling, Turpan) are drawn from other work. Q1 is 'no', so Q2-Q9 are 'no'.
